title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Comms & Templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard incident lifecycle, on-call rotations, runbook templates, postmortem requirements, game day guidance, and communications templates (internal and customer-facing). It is intended for engineers, SREs, support, and on-call responders. Follow this playbook for all incidents impacting production services, region availability, or customer-facing SLAs.

Scope and audience:
- Applies to Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private control plane services.
- Audience: on-call engineers, incident commanders (ICs), support, product & comms leads.

Incident severity definitions:
1) SEV-1 (P0) — Service outage or data loss affecting all or large fraction of customers or causing platform unavailability. Examples: control plane down, model inference 100% errors, major data corruption.
2) SEV-2 (P1) — Significant degradation impacting many customers or critical features (e.g., high error rate / high latency for large subset).
3) SEV-3 (P2) — Partial impact or degraded performance for a small subset of customers; no immediate SLA breach.
4) SEV-4 (P3) — Informational or request for operational change with minor impact.

High-level incident lifecycle (steps):
1) Detect & Triage
   - Alert, customer report, or monitoring anomaly.
   - First responder acknowledges within 5 mins for SEV-1/2, 30 mins for SEV-3.
2) Classify & Escalate
   - Determine SEV, scope, possible blast radius.
   - Notify IC and paging lists per escalation matrix.
3) Respond & Mitigate
   - Run the appropriate runbook (SEV-1 runbook mandatory).
   - Apply mitigations to restore service (fallback model, scale up, traffic reroute).
4) Communicate
   - Post initial incident status to internal channel, incident bridge, and status.redwood.ai.
   - Send customer comms if external impact (see templates).
5) Resolve & Recover
   - Validate fixes, monitor for recurrence.
   - Close incident when service is stable and postmortem is scheduled.
6) Postmortem & Follow-up
   - Execute postmortem template and create action items with owners and due dates.
   - Track remediation in Jira and review in weekly reliability sync.

On-call rotations and responsibilities:
- Primary on-call: first responder for alerts; responsible for initial triage and running runbooks.
- Secondary on-call: backup for escalation and taking over if primary unavailable.
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates responders, public/internal comms, and decisions for mitigation and rollback.
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): invoked as required (runtime, infra, networking, security, data).

Rotation patterns:
- Engineering: 1-week primary rotation, 1-week secondary rotation.
- Shift handover: 15-minute overlap; outgoing engineer must summarize active alerts and ongoing mitigation in on-call Slack channel.
- Escalation rules: if primary does not acknowledge within 10 mins for SEV-1, pager escalates to secondary; if unacked 15 mins, escalates to IC.

SEV-1 runbook (mandatory checklist) — quick reference:
1) Acknowledge alert, join incident bridge (Zoom/Jitsi link).
2) Post the short incident header in #incidents: "SEV-1: [service] — short summary — IC: [name] — <link to bridge>".
3) Triage: check dashboards (latency, error rates, capacity) and recent deploys.
4) Apply immediate mitigations (traffic reroute, autoscale, rollback, switch to fallback model).
5) If mitigation successful, confirm stability for 15 minutes and update status page.
6) If not, escalate to SME and consider progressive rollback or region failover.
7) Document every action in timeline (use the incident document template below).
8) Declare recovery only after monitoring window and stakeholder acknowledgement.

SEV runbook quick commands (examples):
- Check API error rate: kubectl logs -n prod api | grep ERROR | wc -l
- Force revert to last-good model: ./deploy-tool rollback --service=model-serving --revision=rev-2026-02-05
- Scale inference pool: infra-cli autoscale --pool=inference-1 --replicas=50

Incident communication guidelines:
- Internal communications: keep #incidents and triage channel updated every 15 minutes for SEV-1, every 30 minutes for SEV-2. Use clear status lines: Impact, Scope, Mitigation, ETA.
- Customer communications: be factual, avoid speculation, provide ETA if available, and follow up with root cause and remediation timeline in postmortem.
- Public status page: always post an incident entry for SEV-1 and SEV-2 affecting customers. Update every 30 minutes or on state change.

Internal incident message template (Slack & Incident Doc header):
- Title: SEV-[level]: [service] — [short summary]
- Time detected: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
- IC: [name] | Pager: [@handle]
- Impact: [brief sentence: % customers, features affected]
- Current status: Investigating / Mitigating / Restored
- Mitigation in flight: [actions]
- Next update: +15m

Customer-facing email/status template (initial):
Subject: Incident update: [service] — [short summary]
Hello [Customer/Team],

We detected an incident affecting [service] at [time UTC]. Impact: [brief description]. Our engineers are actively investigating and mitigating. We will provide updates every [30 minutes / on significant change].

What we are doing: [short bullet list of mitigations].
Next update: [ETA/time].

We apologize for the impact.
— Redwood Inference Reliability Team

Customer-facing status:update template (follow-up):
Subject: Incident resolved: [service] — [summary of cause]
Hello [Customer/Team],

The incident affecting [service] has been resolved at [time UTC]. Root cause (initial): [one-sentence summary]. Impact: [scope]. Remediation: [what we changed].
Postmortem and preventative actions will be shared within [72 hours].

Thank you for your patience.
— Redwood Inference Reliability Team

Status page content guidelines (status.redwood.ai):
- Incident Title: clear and short (e.g., "Inference API: Increased error rate - SEV-1")
- Impact: one-line summary
- Affected components/regions: list
- Timeline of key events with timestamps (UTC)
- Current status and next steps
- Link to customer communications and postmortem when available

Incident document template (use for every SEV-1/2):
- Title: [SEV level] — [Service] — [Short Summary]
- Incident ID: INC-YYYYMMDD-XX
- Detection time: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
- Resolved time: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
- IC: [name]
- Responders: [list names & roles]
- Impact: [detailed description; metrics if available]
- Timeline: numbered timeline of actions with timestamps
- Root cause: [initial hypothesis and final RCA]
- Mitigation steps taken: [ordered list]
- Customer communications: [links / copy pasted emails]
- Postmortem link: [URL when available]
- Action items: table of action, owner, due date, status

Postmortem template and acceptance criteria:
- Summary (3–5 sentences)
- Impacted customers/features and severity
- Timeline of events
- Root cause analysis (technical and organizational factors)
- Corrective actions (short-term and long-term) with owners and deadlines
- Metrics to validate effectiveness (e.g., error rate, latency)
- Lessons learned and prevention plan
- Acceptance criteria: postmortem must be published within 72 hours for SEV-1 and SEV-2, include at least one measurable remediation, and have a clear owner and due date for each action.

Game day (table-top) checklist:
Pre-game (1 week before):
- Confirm attendees (ICs, SRE, runtime, infra, product).
- Validate monitoring alerts are working and on-call rosters are up to date.
- Prepare a simulated incident scenario and required runbooks.

Play day (exercise):
- Start with a short brief on objectives and success criteria.
- Trigger simulated alert and time the acknowledgement and response.
- Run through SEV-1 runbook actions, communications, and status page updates.
- Observe handoffs and escalation timings.

Post-game (after action):
- Publish a short AAR (after-action review) within 3 days.
- Track game-day action items and close in Jira.

Runbook authoring & maintenance standards:
- Keep runbooks under eng-platform/runbooks and tag with last-updated date.
- Minimum content: purpose, detection signals, step-by-step mitigation commands, rollback steps, validation steps, and post-incident cleanup.
- Runbooks must be reviewed quarterly by owners and after each related incident.
- Add a quick-check table at top: SEV level, estimated mitigation time, SME owners, required credentials.

Escalation matrix (example primary contacts):
- On-call Primary: @oncall-primary (rotate weekly)
- On-call Secondary: @oncall-secondary
- IC escalation: Senior SRE (Marcus Li) — pager: +1-555-0102
- Runtime SME: Sofia Gómez — pager: +1-555-0147
- Cloud & Networking: Daniel Hsu — pager: +1-555-0166

Service-level playbook examples (short):
- Inference API increased error rate:
  1) Confirm spike via metrics: requests/sec, 5xx rate > 2.5% for 10+ minutes
  2) Check recent deploys and rollout status (k8s deployment history)
  3) Temporarily shift traffic to fallback model version or region
  4) Open an incident doc and update status page- Model KV cache bloat causing latency:
  1) Flush cache for affected pods (safe drain)
  2) Reprovision larger cache instance or rollback recent model changes
  3) Monitor heatmap and latency p95

Post-incident follow-up and governance:
- SEV-1/2: postmortem published within 72 hrs, action items tracked and reviewed weekly until closed.
- SEV-3: RCA summary acceptable within 7 days.
- Quarterly reliability review: top incidents, trends, and recurring action items to be presented to execs.

Appendices:
A) Quick-check table (example):
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| SEV | 1 |
| Estimated mitigation | 15–90 minutes |
| Typical IC | Senior SRE |
| Required runbooks | inference-api-sev1, deploy-rollback |

B) Incident timeline example (format):
- 2026-02-10 14:02 UTC — Alert triggered: API 5xx > 20%
- 2026-02-10 14:05 UTC — Primary acknowledged; IC appointed (Aisha Patel)
- 2026-02-10 14:12 UTC — Traffic rerouted to fallback model; 5xx reduced to 1.7%
- 2026-02-10 14:30 UTC — Monitoring window passed; incident declared resolved at 14:35 UTC

C) Templates & snippets (copyable):
- Slack: 'SEV-1: Inference API — increased 5xx — IC: @Aisha — bridge: <link>. Impact: ~65% of customers. Mitigating: rerouting to fallback model. Next update +15m.'
- Status page entry (Markdown):
  Title: Inference API — Increased error rate (Resolved)
  Impact: 5xx errors affecting inference requests in us-east-1; customers experienced increased latency and failures.
  Timeline: [see incident doc]
  Resolution: Traffic rerouted to fallback model; root cause under investigation

D) Ownership and training:
- All on-call engineers must complete incident training and a shadow week before primary rotation.
- New SRE hires must run at least one game day within first 90 days.

E) Contact & escalation quick list:
- Pager duty: https://pager.redwood.ai
- Incident bridge template: https://bridges.redwood.ai/template
- Postmortem board: https://jira.redwood.ai/boards/INC-POSTMORTEMS

If you have questions or proposed updates to this playbook, open a PR against eng-platform/runbooks or contact the owner team (engineering reliability).
